record.original_question: Given an n-dimensional manifold M^n equipped with a metric, develop an effective criterion or procedure for deciding whether that metric can be realized as an isometric embedding of M^n into another manifold of dimension n(n+1)/2.

evidence.quote: One should have an effective way to check whether a metric on M^n can be isometrically embedded into another manifold with dimension n(n+1)/2

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^n, g)$ be a smooth $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with metric $g$. The number $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$ equals the number of independent components of a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor in dimension $n$, and is the natural target dimension associated with the local isometric embedding problem (the Janet–Cartan dimension).

Problem. Develop an effective criterion or decision procedure that, given the metric $g$ on $M^n$ (for instance presented in local coordinates or via its components in some atlas), determines whether there exists an isometric embedding (or immersion) of $(M^n, g)$ into some Riemannian manifold $N$ of dimension $\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$. Here "isometric embedding" means a smooth map $f : M^n \to N$ such that $f^* g_N = g$, where $g_N$ denotes the metric on $N$. The criterion should be effective in the sense that it can be checked by a finite procedure applied to the components of $g$ and their derivatives.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on isometric embeddings (Nash, Janet–Cartan, Gromov, and subsequent work) provides existence theorems and dimension bounds but does not provide an effective decidable criterion for embeddability into a target of dimension n(n+1)/2. Surveys and recent works on the embedding problem continue to treat such effective criteria as outstanding, supporting an open status.

status_evidence.title: Nash embedding theorems - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Nash's theorems guarantee existence of isometric embeddings into Euclidean spaces of certain dimensions, but provide no effective criterion for embeddability into a target of minimal dimension n(n+1)/2.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known with various dimension bounds; an effective criterion in the Janet–Cartan dimension n(n+1)/2 is not established.

status_evidence.title: Isometric Embedding of Riemannian Manifolds in Euclidean Spaces (AMS Surveys)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the isometric embedding problem; describes partial results and open questions about local and global embeddability.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference indicating embedding criteria in low target dimensions remain only partially understood.
